name: Fairmont Empress
positioning: Chateau-style Fairmont hotel overlooking Victoria's Inner Harbour, just steps from downtown
best_for: Travelers who want a harbourfront, walkable base in downtown Victoria
Guests who want a long-running Afternoon Tea tradition
Families who like a hotel kids program

facts.text: The hotel overlooks Victoria's Inner Harbour and is just steps from downtown.
The hotel was named a National Historic Site of Canada in 1981.
Q Bar offers live music every evening.
The Veranda serves signature cocktails and shareable plates on a terrace overlooking the water.
The Signature Harbour View room keeps original architectural features such as graceful arches, circular turret seating nooks and crown molding.
There is an indoor heated swimming pool and whirlpool, plus a wading pool for young children.
The Kids Rule the Castle program includes an activity book with a scavenger hunt through the hotel and complimentary milk and cookies in the room.
The hotel is a stone's throw from the seaplane terminal for flights to Vancouver.
A rooftop herb garden supplies herbs used in the hotel's menus.

highlights.text: The hotel has been pouring traditional Afternoon Tea in Victoria for well over a century.
British architect Francis Rattenbury designed the chateau-style hotel, which is named after Queen Victoria.
Fairmont Gold guests have access to a lounge overlooking the Inner Harbour, evening canapes and private check-in.
The hotel makes its own 1908 Indigo Gin, which changes color depending on what it is mixed with.
Q at the Empress serves seasonally inspired menus celebrating Pacific Northwest cuisine.

considerations.text: Bathrooms can be on the small side and not all of them have tubs.
Afternoon tea is described as pricey.
WhataHotel notes that some rooms in the historic building have smaller footprints and varying layouts.
